exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
outcome: Change in platelet count from day 0 to day 2 (ΔPlt [D 0-2])
Change in platelet count from day 0 to day 5 (ΔPlt [D 0-5])
cohort: 41 mothers with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) and their 65 infants born by vaginal delivery (VD, n = 30) and cesarean section (CS, n = 35) between January 1997 and March 2022.
finding: In infants born to mothers with immune thrombocytopenia, vaginal delivery was associated with a significantly greater decrease in platelet count from birth to day 2 and day 5 compared to cesarean section.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery (VD) was associated with a significantly greater decrease in platelet count compared to cesarean section (CS).
